thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered: LB-targets-unhealthy (prod-eu) — 3/5 targets failing health checks, TLS handshake errors up to 27% 

pagerduty: Incident created: PD-48921. Urgency: high. Notify: #incidents, roxanne_oncall (primary), sam_sre (secondary)

roxanne_oncall: I’m on it. grabbing logs from edge and ALB now. anyone seeing customer reports?

emily_support: Getting ~15 tickets mentioning ‘failed to connect’ and some errors showing in-app with "TLS handshake failed". Sending a short status to affected customers now.

sam_sre: Observing spike of 502/503s from eu-edge. ALB target group tg-eu-prod shows 3/5 targets Unhealthy, health check path /_hc returns 502. TLS handshake error in ALB logs: "tls: handshake failure: no certificate" for a subset of clients (SNI present).

tonny_netops: tagging in—checking certs and host level. certs for edge rotated yesterday but only on canary hosts? pulling cert rotation job logs.

jess_eng: running quick curl to the ALB ip to reproduce: ```curl -vk https://prod-eu.example.com/ -I``` returns: ```* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1) * TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2) * TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS alert, Alert number 70 * SSL connection using TLSv1.3 / AEAD etc. HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable```

karim_engops: ok that matches. ALB logs show backend returned 503 with connection errors: "write tcp x.x.x.x:443: write: broken pipe". health check failures look like envoy rejecting TLS because backend presents a cert with CN=internal not expected SNI.

roxanne_oncall: hypothesis: partial cert rotation combined with an envoy config rollout left some targets using legacy certs — SNI mismatch with ALB health checks causing TLS abort, health checks fail -> targets marked unhealthy -> traffic shifts -> customer errors.

sam_sre: Confirmed: old certs present on hosts i-0a,b,c. New cert present on i-0d,e. Rotation job shows error for i-0a earlier: "permission denied writing /etc/ssl/certs/.." — ops script aborted but returned success to orchestrator.

jess_eng: immediate mitigation: we can shift traffic weights away from tg-eu-prod to tg-eu-fallback (healthy region pool) while we fix certs. That will reduce latency for some EU customers but stop failures. Anyone object?

emily_support: go for it — we notified customers about partial outage; minimizing errors will reduce ticket spike.

tonny_netops: executing weight shift via route-control: ```aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn arn:.. --default-actions '[{"Type":"forward","ForwardConfig":{"TargetGroups":[{"TargetGroupArn":"tg-eu-fallback","Weight":80},{"TargetGroupArn":"tg-eu-prod","Weight":20}]}}]'``` will do gradual shift.

incident-bot: Action logged: traffic-weight-change initiated by tonny_netops — request id rc-2026-07. Auto rollback at 10m if error.

roxanne_oncall: performing a quick cert remediate on the failed hosts in parallel (ssh + agent). @karim_engops will you re-run rotation with debug flags to surface the failure cause?

karim_engops: re-run started with `cert-rotate --hosts i-0a,i-0b,i-0c --verbose --dry-run=false` — hitting same permission error on i-0a. escalating to infra team, looks like a stale IAM role on that host preventing writes to the mounted KMS agent socket.

sam_sre: while infra fixes role, we should also relax ALB health check strictness to allow ephemeral TLS negotiation quirks to pass — change expected response from 200 to 2xx/3xx for short window. That will keep targets in service if TLS completes. Thoughts?

tonny_netops: we can update health check matcher: ```aws elbv2 modify-target-group-health-check --target-group-arn tg-eu-prod --matcher HttpCode=200,302``` — but careful: might hide real failures. use for 5-10 minutes only.

roxanne_oncall: do both: weight shift + temporary health matcher + infra fix. I'm going to page infra and cert-owner on rotation. @sam_sre can you monitor 5m windows and decide rollback?

sam_sre: monitoring logs now. after weight shift we see error rate drop from 26% -> 6% in 2 minutes. ticket velocity dropping. health check success on i-0d,e remains, i-0a-c flapping.

emily_support: update sent to customers: "We are investigating intermittent connection failures in EU. Mitigation in progress; some traffic routed to fallback nodes. We'll send another update in 30 minutes."

karim_engops: infra fixed IAM role on i-0a and re-ran rotation, cert now present and served. verifying with openssl: ```openssl s_client -connect i-0a:443 -servername prod-eu.example.com | openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer``` shows CN=prod-eu cert issued by Redwood CA.

jess_eng: re-checking ALB health: i-0a,b,c reporting healthy now. Running couple of synthetic requests: success. Rolling weights back to normal over 5 min.

incident-bot: Action logged: health-check-matcher-restored by sam_sre; traffic-weight-change rollback scheduled and executed by tonny_netops.

sam_sre: Post-mitigation numbers: error rate down to baseline ~0.5%. 3rd party monitoring shows full recovery. No data loss.

roxanne_oncall: Great work. I’ll keep this thread open for post-incident notes. Assigning follow-ups: 1) cert-rotation job: harden error detection + fail job on non-zero exit (karim_engops) 2) rotation runbook: add IAM validation pre-check (tonny_netops) 3) ALB health-check playbook: include safe matcher rollback checklist (jess_eng).

emily_support: Filing a summarised customer-facing postmortem for CS. Will include timeline and support actions.

karim_engops: will open a PR with stricter return-code checks and add unit tests against iam-mock.

roxanne_oncall: handoff to follow-up owner: karim_engops for 12h. If anything spikes escalate to sam_sre. Closing alert in PD. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty: Incident PD-48921 acknowledged by roxanne_oncall and resolved by sam_sre.

roxanne_oncall: closing the thread — summary to be posted to /incidents/postmortems after writeup. Thanks all :pray:
